summary: The article profiles how local amateur teams, led by the Rosedale Raptors and Coach Marcus Redwood, promote sportsmanship, highlighted by a viral post-tackle apology called 'The Handshake That Healed.' It draws on coaches, a sports psychologist, team captains and parents to show how respect and integrity build character, life skills and community bonds. It concludes that balancing competitiveness with sportsmanship defines respected teams.
one_line: Local amateur teams like the Rosedale Raptors show how sportsmanship builds character, community bonds and respect, exemplified by the viral 'Handshake That Healed.'
key_facts: The Rosedale Raptors, a local soccer team that plays at Rosedale Park, are coached by Marcus Redwood, a former semi-professional player.
Marcus Redwood says, "Sportsmanship is the soul of the game."
On October 13th, 2023, a Raptors player accidentally tackled Alex Porter, captain of the rival Maplewood Marauders, during a heated match.
Raptors midfielder Jamie Linton offered Alex Porter a handshake and an apology after Redwood called the tackling player to the sidelines to remind him of the team's ethos.
The handshake was filmed on a spectator's smartphone, went viral, and became known as 'The Handshake That Healed.'
Sara Jennings, a local sports psychologist, has worked with the Raptors and other local teams since July 2024 and says sportsmanship "shapes character."
The Raptors are active in local charities and youth clinics, spreading the message of sportsmanship off the field.
Karen Thompson is captain of the Westburg Women's Basketball Association, established September 2023, whose players juggle careers and families.
On November 2nd, 2023, the Westburg Warriors helped an injured opponent off the court and forfeited a strategic advantage.
John and Lisa Garfield, parents of twin boys in the Littleton Youth Soccer League, said in a December 18th, 2023 interview that their sons developed respect for teammates and competitors.
Elizabeth Meyers, a former national swimmer, has coached the Eastville Swim Team since its founding on September 12th, 2024.
Eastville swimmers have a tradition of applauding all competitors after each race, regardless of the outcome.
